messages.content: Phoenix is wrapped, so I am moving to Kansas City. I need flights and a hotel for March 24-26 from Chicago. Agenda: public art campus tour Thursday morning, library partner Thursday afternoon, and a Friday debrief that should end before noon. I would like to avoid a rental car if rideshares and hotel location make sense, keep the room near the grant travel guidance, and come home Friday after lunch. For hotels, please note breakfast, room coffee/fridge if shown, and easy dinner nearby.

Happy to. To compare the hotel areas accurately, do you have the neighborhoods or cross streets for the campus, library, and debrief? Also, what is the nightly guidance number, and is ORD preferred over Midway?

Grant guidance says try to stay under about $180 before taxes unless the block or location justifies it. The campus is around 31st and Troost, the library meeting is at the downtown central library, and the Friday debrief is likely in Crossroads. ORD is easier than Midway, but I would use Midway for a big savings. Economy is fine. United is nice if comparable, but not at the expense of Friday timing.
Got it. I will treat this as a no-car plan unless the local timing looks strained. I will compare ORD nonstops first, then check Midway only if it changes the total meaningfully.
Also, I want enough margin Wednesday to check in and eat early. I am not trying to land at 8 p.m.

Here is a compact first pass, assuming fares are still live:
| Option | Flights | Air est. | Why it fits | Trade-off |
| A | United ORD-MCI 11:55a-1:31p; MCI-ORD 2:40p-4:10p | $318 | Best balance: early check-in margin and after-lunch return | Tight if Friday lunch drifts past 1:20 |
| B | American ORD-MCI 1:05p-2:43p; MCI-ORD 4:35p-6:05p | $286 | Cheaper and more Friday airport cushion | Later Chicago arrival, less afternoon setup time |
| C | Southwest MDW-MCI 10:25a-12:05p; MCI-MDW 3:20p-4:55p | $304 | Good times; checked bags included | Only worth it if Midway is not a hassle |
I would ignore the connecting itineraries unless the fare gap gets much larger; most arrive late or save under $60.
Can you layer in hotel areas and airport/local transport? The no-car question is the main thing.

Hotel-area view:
| Area | Est. 2-night room+tax | Meeting access | Hotel practicalities | Dinner | Bottom line |
| Crossroads limited-service | $400-$420 | 12-15 min to campus, 5-8 min to library, likely walk or short ride to Friday debrief | Often includes breakfast; coffee maker and mini-fridge commonly listed, but verify | Several casual spots within a few blocks | Best no-car base |
| Downtown/Library district full-service | $345-$390 | Walk or very short ride to library; 15-18 min to campus; 5-10 min to Crossroads | Breakfast often extra; fridge may be by request | On-site restaurant plus nearby options | Lower rate, more amenity uncertainty |
| Plaza/Westport | $370-$415 | 7-10 min to campus; 15-20 min to library/Crossroads | Mixed breakfast setup; some suite options | Strong dinner choices | Good for campus, weaker for the full agenda |
What would the rideshare math look like if I skipped the car?

Rough no-car ground estimate: MCI to hotel $38-$48 each way; hotel to campus Thursday $16-$22; campus to library $14-$18; library or debrief local hop $8-$14; hotel to MCI Friday $38-$48. Total is about $115-$150 if the host covers one hop, or $150-$180 if every leg is yours. A compact rental for two days is likely $170-$210 plus downtown parking, so no car is cheaper and simpler unless the Thursday campus location moves farther out.
Good. I may have host help between the Thursday meetings, but not guaranteed. Is Crossroads close enough that an 8:30 arrival at the campus is realistic?

Yes, with normal traffic. From Crossroads, I would request the ride around 8:00 for an 8:30 campus arrival. The drive is roughly 12-15 minutes, but I would give it 25-30 minutes door-to-door. Downtown is similar but a few minutes farther; Plaza is closer to campus but worse for Friday debrief and airport timing.

Which specific hotels would you shortlist? I would rather have breakfast included and a coffee maker and mini-fridge in the room if available. Nearby dinner matters Wednesday because I will not have a car.

Specific shortlist I would price-check now:
| Hotel | Rate feel | Breakfast / room notes | Why keep it |
| Hampton Inn & Suites Kansas City Downtown Crossroads | About $172-$178 pre-tax | Breakfast included; coffee maker and mini-fridge listed on most standard rooms | Best fit for no car, early Thursday, simple Friday |
| Home2 Suites or similar extended-stay downtown/Crossroads | About $180-$190 pre-tax | Breakfast included; larger fridge or kitchenette style | Very practical, but may exceed guidance |
| Hotel Kansas City or Hotel Phillips downtown | About $145-$165 pre-tax | Breakfast usually not included; coffee/fridge should be confirmed | Cheaper and dinner is easy, but less self-sufficient |
Is the airport area worth considering for savings?

No. An airport hotel at $120-$135 could save about $70-$100 before local trips, but it adds a long Thursday morning ride, leaves you detached from dinner options, and does not help the downtown library or Crossroads debrief. Once you add extra rideshares, the savings mostly disappears.
Could you put the two best whole-trip totals together: Crossroads with the midafternoon United return versus downtown with the cheaper American return?

| Plan | Air | Hotel | Ground | Breakfast gap | Est. total | Timing/trade-off |
| Crossroads + United | $318 | $410 | $150 | $0 | About $878 | Arrive 1:31p Wednesday and back to Chicago 4:10p Friday; costlier but cleanest no-car setup |
| Downtown full-service + American | $286 | $360 | $160 | $30-$40 | About $836-$846 | Cheaper and more Friday airport cushion; later return and less certainty on room amenities |
The true difference is probably $30-$45, not the full hotel-rate gap, once breakfast and local movement are included.
That helps. What would you do at this stage?

I would hold a refundable Crossroads limited-service room if it is still near $175-$180 pre-tax. It protects the no-car plan, keeps Wednesday dinner easy, and avoids paying for breakfast elsewhere. Then ticket flights once the Friday debrief/lunch timing is firm: United if it remains around the low $300s with the 2:40 return; American if you want the cheaper fare and extra Friday cushion. Skip the rental car for now. Before entering the card, verify total with taxes, cancellation deadline, included breakfast, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, and Friday bag storage.

messages.content: Update on Kansas City: the host moved the Thursday pickup earlier, around 8:05, and can collect me only from downtown or Crossroads. I narrowed the hotel choices to the Hampton in Crossroads at $176 and Hotel Kansas City downtown at $149. Can you compare the real difference after taxes and local transportation?
Yes. Are both for March 24-26 and refundable? If you have the taxes/fees and cancellation lines from the booking pages, I can make the comparison tighter.

Both are two nights. Hampton shows $176 nightly, $61 in taxes/fees, refundable until March 22 at 6 p.m. Hotel Kansas City shows $149 nightly, $56 in taxes/fees, cancel by March 21 at noon. Hotel Kansas City says room amenities vary and breakfast is not included, but it has an on-site restaurant.

| Choice | Lodging total | Likely local transport | Breakfast add-on | Thursday pickup | Room/cancel notes | Practical total |
| Hampton Crossroads | $413 | $145-$165 | $0 | Lobby pickup around 8:05 works | Breakfast included; verify coffee maker and mini-fridge; cancel Mar. 22 by 6 p.m. | $558-$578 |
| Hotel Kansas City downtown | $354 | $155-$175 | $32-$42 for two mornings | I would be downstairs by 7:50-7:55 because of the downtown pickup loop | Coffee/fridge uncertain; cancel Mar. 21 by noon | $541-$571 |
So the downtown option is only about $7-$37 cheaper once breakfast and slightly more local movement are included.
That is a much smaller gap than the nightly rate makes it look like.

Exactly. The $54 pre-tax room savings shrinks because the Crossroads rate buys back breakfast and reduces uncertainty. The downtown hotel is still defensible if you value the on-site restaurant, but it does not clearly solve the early pickup or room-amenity questions.
Does the on-site restaurant make downtown better for Wednesday dinner? I am arriving early evening, so simple is good.

It helps, but I would not let it decide this one. From the Crossroads Hampton, you should have several casual dinner choices within a short walk or very short ride. If the weather is bad, downtown's on-site restaurant is more convenient, but Crossroads still has enough nearby that you are not stranded.
What room details should I confirm before booking Hampton? I want a standard one-bed room if possible.

Before you submit, confirm: one-bed queen or king room, breakfast included and the start time, in-room coffee maker, mini-fridge, total charge of $413 or close to it, refundable cancellation through March 22 at 6 p.m., and whether they can store your bag on Friday after checkout.
If the fridge is not shown on the final page but the hotel site lists it, would you still book?

Yes, if the final page still shows the right room and refundable terms. I would add a note requesting the mini-fridge and then call or message the hotel to confirm it. I would not switch to the downtown full-service option just because the Hampton booking engine is vague on that line.
Okay. Is the Crossroads reservation the more practical one even though it is a little higher?

Yes. Book the refundable Hampton Crossroads if the total and cancellation line still match. The small all-in premium is easy to justify because it protects the host pickup, includes breakfast, keeps the room setup more predictable, and keeps dinner options close without adding a rental car. Save the itemized confirmation, cancellation deadline, and amenity notes for reimbursement.

messages.content: Kansas City hotel is reserved in Crossroads. The Friday debrief is now confirmed for 10:30 to noon, and the casual lunch will probably run until about 1:15. Can we pick the flights? I need to arrive Wednesday with time to check in and eat, depart Friday only after lunch, and avoid a late return to Chicago.
Yes. For the Friday return, are you comfortable leaving the Crossroads area around 1:30 if lunch ends at 1:15, or do you want a wider buffer?
Leaving around 1:30 is fine if the flight is after about 3. I will have only a carry-on. I do not want a connection unless the savings are really meaningful.

Refreshed short list:
| Option | Itinerary | Fare | Friday airport margin | Chicago return | Take |
| United nonstop | ORD-MCI 11:55a-1:31p; MCI-ORD 3:05p-4:36p | $326 | Leave Crossroads 1:30-1:35; about 70-85 min at MCI | Earliest home | Cleanest choice |
| American nonstop | ORD-MCI 1:05p-2:43p; MCI-ORD 5:10p-6:42p | $292 | Very comfortable | Early evening | Good fallback |
| Delta connect via MSP | ORD-MCI 10:20a-2:05p; MCI-ORD 4:45p-8:58p | $238 | Fine, but long | Late | Cheap but inefficient |
Is that 3:05 United return too tight if lunch runs to 1:20?

It is workable, not luxurious. If you are in the rideshare by 1:30-1:35, you should reach MCI around 2:00-2:10. With a carry-on and mobile boarding pass, that gives a reasonable buffer for a 3:05 departure. I would not choose it if you expected a checked bag or a formal lunch that could drift much later.
The connection saves almost $90. Is that worth considering?

I would not take the connection for this trip. It adds a delay point and gets you back to Chicago more than four hours later than the United nonstop. The nonstop premium is easy to explain because it protects the Friday agenda and avoids a late return.
Then I will ticket United if it is still under $340. Anything specific to watch on the purchase page?

Ticket the United nonstops if the fare is still around $326 and under $340: ORD-MCI arriving about 1:31 p.m. Wednesday, and MCI-ORD departing about 3:05 p.m. Friday. Before paying, confirm both legs are nonstop, the fare is not basic economy if your office restricts it, carry-on and seat-selection rules are acceptable, the dates are March 24 and 26, and the change/cancel terms fit reimbursement policy. If the fare jumps well above $340, pause and compare the American nonstop before buying.
